paragraphs: The S500 has been part of the S-Class range since 2008. Early and mid-generation cars (W221 and W222, roughly 2008 to 2017) use the M278 — a 4.7-litre V8 petrol engine. From 2020, the W223-generation S500 switched to the M256, a newer 3.0-litre straight-six with mild-hybrid assistance. Knowing which one your car has matters, because the components, the known wear pattern, and even the rebuild cost differ between them — which is exactly why we confirm your exact engine by registration before quoting.
about.boldParagraph: We continue to rebuild and replace M256 engines for every S500 on the road.

cards.body: A 4.7-litre V8 petrol fitted to the S500 from 2008 to 2017, across two generations. Known for timing chain wear and coolant system issues over time — see the callout above. We replace timing chains, valve seals and coolant system components as standard on every M278 rebuild.
A 3.0-litre inline-six petrol with mild-hybrid assistance, fitted from 2020. This is a modern, generally reliable engine that doesn't share the same known issues as the older M278 V8.

compatibility.intro: Because the S500 spans two distinct engines across three generations, fitting the wrong replacement — or assuming an M278 part will work on an M256 car — risks a compatibility problem that's expensive to unpick. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm:

points.text: Your exact engine code (M256) via registration or VIN
Any electronics or ECU considerations specific to your exact build

compatibility.footer: This is why we always start with your registration rather than a generic S-Class quote — it protects you from paying for parts that don't fit your actual car.
